issues.legal_issue: A protected tenancy status that accrued under a repealed law remained an accrued right despite the repeal.
material_facts: The tenants met the conditions for protected status under the earlier tenancy law, and that status was recorded in the official record of rights.
The landlord did not apply through the procedure provided by the earlier law to have the tenants declared not to be protected tenants.
issues.conclusion: The tenants' protected status had accrued before repeal and was preserved by the saving provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3A(1) of the Bombay Tenancy Act, 1939, as amended, protected status arose by operation of law unless the landlord sought a declaration to the contrary; section 89(2)(b)(i) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 preserved rights already acquired or accrued. The Court distinguished Abbot v. The Minister for Lands, [1895] A.C. 425: a mere unexercised opportunity to acquire a right is not an accrued right, whereas the tenants' status had already vested without further action on their part and was officially recorded.

predicates.protected_tenancy_repeal_dispute: The dispute concerns a claim to protected tenancy status following repeal of the law under which that status could arise.
predicates.protected_status_accrued_before_repeal: The tenants acquired protected status under the earlier law before its repeal, and the status was recorded officially.

issues.definition: When a protected-tenancy dispute follows repeal and the tenants' status had already accrued, that status is preserved.

issues.legal_issue: A later law's exclusion of specified land from its provisions does not extinguish protected tenancy status that accrued before the law took effect.
material_facts: The land fell within an area excluded from the operation of the later tenancy law.
The tenants had acquired protected status under the earlier law before the later law came into force.
issues.conclusion: The exclusion applied prospectively and did not take away the tenants' previously accrued protected status.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 88(1) and 89(2)(b)(i) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, read with section 31, did not show an intention to confiscate accrued status. The Court held that the exclusions in section 88 operated from the commencement of the 1948 Act and did not divest rights already preserved by section 89.

predicates.protected_tenancy_repeal_dispute: The dispute concerns a claim to protected tenancy status following repeal of the law under which that status could arise.
predicates.land_excluded_from_new_law: The land is of a kind that the later law excludes from its substantive provisions.
predicates.protected_status_accrued_before_new_law: The tenants acquired protected status under the earlier law before the later law came into force.

issues.definition: If a protected-tenancy dispute concerns land excluded from a later law and the status accrued before that law, the exclusion does not extinguish the prior status.

issues.legal_issue: A proceeding concerning a right preserved on repeal must be resolved under the repealed law when the saving provision so directs.
material_facts: The tenants claimed a protected right acquired under the earlier tenancy law.
The landlord brought a possession suit concerning that right after the later tenancy law had replaced the earlier law.
issues.conclusion: The dispute had to be resolved under the earlier law, and the suit for possession was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 89(2)(b)(ii) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, required proceedings in respect of a preserved right to be continued and disposed of as if the later Act had not been passed. The Court held that this provision did not limit the independent preservation of accrued rights under section 89(2)(b)(i), and that the present controversy was to be resolved under the Bombay Tenancy Act, 1939. It considered the difference from section 7 of the Bombay General Clauses Act but found that it did not change this result.

predicates.proceeding_over_repeal_saved_right: The case is a legal proceeding concerning a right claimed to have been preserved when the law creating it was repealed.
predicates.proceeding_concerns_preexisting_tenancy_: The proceeding concerns a tenancy right acquired before the later law came into force.

issues.definition: A proceeding concerning a tenancy right acquired before the later law is resolved under the prior law when the repeal preserves that right and directs that such proceedings be disposed of as if the later law had not been passed.
